name: The Data League — data comparison showdowns (football-first)
_channel: The Data League (@thedataleague). Broadcast-style comparisons: two rivals fight across 8 scored rounds of verified statistics, narrated like a title fight. Tagline: 'Every debate ends in a score.' Sign-off: 'And the numbers have spoken.'
_origin: Created 2026-08-17 from the channel strategy doc: football-first niche, season + Championship Belt continuity, Moment-Class commentary engine, two-source data rule, 45-60s Shorts. THIS FILE is the channel's format contract. The Moment-Class engine below IS the commentary IP — every script picks a class per data event.
audience: global football fans 18-34 (LatAm, MENA, South Asia, Europe, Africa) plus the general 'who's better?' argument audience via Shorts. Tribal, argumentative, comment-active.

stakes: He Led For 14 Years. Then THIS Happened.
The Last Time You'll See This Debate

rules: Must accurately describe the video — never clickbait. High CTR + low retention is demoted by YouTube; the promise must land.
Every launch video in the first season carries the final scoreline when it is a marquee match ('The Result: 6-4').
The championship belt is mentioned in the title when it is on the line.

structure.note: Start at the most dramatic moment of the whole video. One line, then the chart is already animating. NO channel intro, NO rules explanation up front.
Establish who is fighting, what is measured, the period, the belt at stake. Max 30 seconds. Commentator voice, not instruction manual.
Quick WOW category (career totals, biggest single number). Instant gratification. Scoreboard updates.
Legacy category. Establish the scoreline direction.
MARQUEE round — the closest, most contested category. Designed for a lead change. Retention peak.
Marquee/volatile category. Second lead change slot.
Volatile/global category (followers, search interest). Upset territory.
Upset or wildcard category. The share spike. If the underdog is winning, this is where it lands.
DOUBLE POINTS. Engineered comeback potential. Sudden-death tiebreak if level. Belt reveal + celebration on winner.

60-90s conclusion: what the data actually says, why it happened, the belt handover. Then the mandatory CTA: subscribe (primary), comment your take + 'who should fight next?' poll (secondary). End on the sign-off: 'And the numbers have spoken.'

voice_rules: THE COMMENTATOR IS 'THE SCOREKEEPER' — the permanent channel voice. Same ElevenLabs voice on every video, forever.
NEVER read raw numbers in speech. Round to 3 significant figures ('15.2 million', not '15,198,432'). The chart shows full precision — the ear gets the round number, the eye gets the truth.
Every round's data event gets a Moment-Class call (see moment_classes below). One class per event, phrase picked from that class's library.
0.3-0.8s of silence before every big reveal. Silence is the strongest tool.
Pace 4-6 words per second. Volume dynamics between classes. Never flat.
Fairness is personality: gloat slightly for the underdog, never cruel to the loser. Both fanbases must feel welcome — that is what makes comments an engagement engine.
Every number carries its source spoken aloud at least once per video: 'per Transfermarkt', 'per FBref', 'per official club filings'.
If two sources disagree, SAY SO on air: 'Transfermarkt says 90, Opta says 91 — we used 90, shown here.'
script.honesty_guard: NEVER invent a statistic for entertainment. Every number must be verified against at least two independent sources, date-stamped, and recorded in the video's data sheet. Net worths and estimates are ALWAYS labelled 'estimate' on air. If a stat is uncertain, say the uncertainty. Corrections become content: pin the correction comment and re-record the line.
script._recency_note: Date-stamp every video ('data as of [date]'). Live statistics (followers, search interest) are snapshots — re-verify anything older than ~48h at write time.

round_rules.tiebreak: sudden-death single category if level after round 8
round_rules.category_mix: at least one each of: legacy (career totals), peak (best single season), velocity (first to reach X), global (followers/search), projection (who's on track by 2030), wildcard (surprise stat)
round_rules.ordering: round 1 = biggest single wow number; rounds 4-5 = the closest categories (retention peak); rounds 6-7 = upsets; round 8 = double points

images.style: dark arena broadcast: deep navy-black floor, volt/cyan neon, Anton caps, JetBrains Mono numbers, combatant color zones. NO photos of players/clubs — stylised silhouettes + colour fields only. NO footage.
images._facts_go_on_cards: All numbers live on the chart-kit components (RaceLine, Scoreboard, H2HMeter, Counter). Atmosphere layers only as background.

sound._note: 3-note sonic logo (whistle -> brass hit) on every scoreboard update. Crowd under celebrations only. Silence before reveals.

voice.tone: title-fight commentator: auctioneer + radio commentator + game show host
voice.tts_voice_hint: ONE permanent ElevenLabs voice — the channel identity. Do not change per video. Do not use a different voice for Shorts.

moment_classes._note: THE COMMENTARY IP. Every data event in a round maps to exactly one class; pick a phrase from that class's library (or write a variant in the same register). Classes are keyed by data conditions, not by vibe.

C0_COLD_OPEN.trigger: video opening line, before the race starts
phrases: For fourteen years, he never lost this race. Then 2023 happened.
Every single number said this was over. Every single number was wrong.
They start level. They do not finish level.
This is the rivalry the internet was built for.

C1_OVERTAKE.delivery: peak volume, 1s of silence before the line
phrases: HE'S DONE IT! [NAME] HAS TAKEN THE LEAD!
AND JUST LIKE THAT — THE LEAD CHANGES HANDS!
OVERTAKE! [NAME] STORMS IN FRONT!
THE LEAD IS GONE. THE LEAD IS [NAME]'S!

C2_GAP_CLOSING.trigger: chaser's velocity exceeds the leader's (the gap is shrinking)
phrases: [NAME] is gaining [N] a week. They are eating the lead.
The gap is coming down. It's coming down fast.
[NAME] is closing — and the leader knows it.
Look at the angle of that line. That is a chase.

C3_BLOWOUT.trigger: gap exceeds ~35% of the leader's value
C3_BLOWOUT.delivery: flat, almost bored — the bigger insult
phrases: This isn't a contest anymore. It's a coronation.
[NAME] has left the building. The rest is a formality.
The numbers aren't close. They never were.
At this point we're just counting the margin.

C4_COMEBACK.trigger: a side that trailed by >30% has now taken the lead
C4_COMEBACK.delivery: highest energy; longest pause before the last word
phrases: FROM [N] BEHIND — THE COMEBACK IS COMPLETE!
They were written off. They did not read the script.
THE BIGGEST COMEBACK THIS CHANNEL HAS EVER SEEN!
Down by a mile. Won by an inch. That's [NAME].

C5_PHOTO_FINISH.trigger: final gap under ~1% of the winner's value
C5_PHOTO_FINISH.delivery: whisper after shout — the contrast is the drama
phrases: Look at the gap. LOOK. AT. THE. GAP.
That is the closest race we have ever broadcast.
A [N] difference. After [YEARS] years. [N].
They are separated by less than the error in the data.

C6_RECORD.trigger: a value crosses the historical maximum of the data set
phrases: That has never been done. By anyone. Ever.
We are watching a record — live, on this chart.
[NAME] just walked past every number in history.
The chart ran out of scale. We had to redraw it.

C7_UPSET.trigger: a side with <25% pre-match probability wins the round
phrases: Wait. WAIT. Nobody gave them a chance. Nobody.
THE UPSET IS REAL! [NAME] HAS DONE IT!
The favourite has been knocked out. In one round.
If you predicted this, you should buy a lottery ticket.
We're going to sudden death.
Level. After everything. Level.
The data refuses to pick a winner. So we go again.
A draw — and this broadcast has no draws.
Everything comes down to this. One category. Two points.
This is what the whole broadcast was building to.
The belt is on the line. Both sides know it.
Win this and it's yours. Lose it and it's gone.
The data doesn't just name a winner — it tells you why.
[NAME] takes it, [SCORE]. But the margin tells the real story.
Both of them won tonight. Only one gets the belt.
And the numbers have spoken.

shorts._note: 45-60s hero Shorts per vidIQ 331M-Short analysis (45-59s = highest avg views, ~70% more likely to reach 1M+ than 15-29s). One category + one reveal per Short. Hook in first 2s. Loopable endings. Comment-bait question at the end + verbal bridge to the long-form.
structures: single-category showdown: cold-open line -> setup -> chase -> reveal -> comment bait
the one-stat Short: one number so absurd it carries the whole Short
the comeback Short: deficit -> overtake -> freeze frame on the gap
the upset Short: build the favourite up, then flip it
shorts.cadence: 3-5 Shorts per long-form + 2 standalone per week

thumbnail.template: dark arena bg, two combatant color zones split left/right, giant scoreboard number between them, max 3 elements, belt emblem when the belt is on the line. Same layout every video = brand recognition.
rules: <=3 visual elements (more = ~23% lower CTR per 2026 studies)
no player photographs — stylised silhouettes/colour fields
numbers in JetBrains Mono, names in Anton

title_rules: Accurate promise, never clickbait. YouTube demotes high-CTR low-retention videos.
A/B test every thumbnail with YouTube's Thumbnail Test & Compare (optimises watch time, not CTR — that is the correct objective).
packaging.viral_gate: Run tools/viral_packaging_engine.py on every video before upload; candidate must score >= 90/100.

season_system._note: The return-audience engine. Every showdown winner takes the Championship Belt. The next video opens with the belt holder defending it. A season table tracks scores across videos. Season 1 = 'The Rivalries': Messi-Ronaldo, Mbappe-Haaland, Brazil-Argentina, Real Madrid-Man City, El Clasico.
rules: Every video's winner takes the belt; next video is a title defense.
Community polls decide the next contender (engagement + data + ownership).
Grand Final at season end: viewer-voted matchup, double points.
Commentary references last season and the belt's history — inside-baseball that builds a community.
TWO-SOURCE RULE: every category verified against two independent sources. Disagreements are said on air.
Public data sheet per video (Google Sheet or GitHub) linked in the description, date-stamped, every number.
Standard date format; 'data as of [date]' chip on every video.
Corrections: pinned comment + annotation + updated sheet. Corrections are content, not shame.
Uncertain numbers always labelled on air: 'estimated', 'reported', 'pre-transfer-fee era'.
